summary: Bhatt and Mathew identify the syntomic complexes Z/p^n(i)_X of Bhatt–Lurie with p-adic étale Tate twists. They introduce F-smooth rings: p-quasisyntomic rings for which each divided Frobenius φ_i : N^iΔ → Δ̄{i} has fibre of p-complete Tor-amplitude ≥ i + 2 and the Nygaard filtration is complete. They show that regular noetherian rings are F-smooth, and that p-complete noetherian F-smooth rings are regular (Theorem 4.15). For a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme, Z/p^n(i)_X agrees with τ^{≤i}Rj_*μ_{p^n}^{⊗i} below degree i, and in degree i with the subsheaf generated by symbols (Theorem 1.8). Consequences: the comparison with Sato's twists for regular semistable schemes (Theorem 5.8), a cohomological-dimension bound for Hodge–Tate stacks of F-finite regular local rings (Corollary 4.20, Bhatt–Lurie's Conjecture 10.1 in that case), and F-smooth = Cartier smooth in characteristic p. The tools are the classes v_1 and θ̃ in the syntomic and Nygaard cohomology of Z_p, a Nygaard filtration on Hodge–Tate cohomology, the étale comparison in the form 'invert v_1', and Bloch–Kato's symbols. The atlas plans the prismatic, Nygaard, Bhatt–Lurie and syntomic inputs (PrismaticCohomology PR.1–PR.5, DerivedDeRhamCohomology). The paper's own theory goes to a new Part II of PrismaticCohomology. Bloch–Kato's nearby-cycle theorems go to the Kato–Swan Part II proposed by the Bright–Newton extraction, and the commutative algebra (Cohen, Avramov, André, Kunz, Popescu, factoriality) to sources of existing layers. Eight mistakes are recorded. One is a gap: in the proof of Theorem 5.8, R[1/p]^× = π^Z × R^× fails at points on several components of the special fibre. The others are misprints: the weight in the equalizer for F_p(i)(A), equation (10), a cross-reference to Proposition 4.6, two wrong theorem numbers in citations, and two slips of wording.

items.name: The étale syntomic complexes Z/p^n(i)_X
items.statement: For a scheme X and i ∈ Z, Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D(X_et, Z/p^n) is the restriction to the small étale site of the syntomic complexes Z/p^n(i)(−) of Bhatt–Lurie [BL22a, §8] (the reduction mod p^n of Z_p(i)(−), defined in the p-complete derived ∞-category), so that RΓ(X, Z/p^n(i)_X) ≃ Z/p^n(i)(X). On affine schemes X ↦ Z/p^n(i)(X) carries filtered colimits of rings to filtered colimits [BL22a, Cor. 8.4.11].
items.note: PR.4 builds the syntomic/Tate-twist fibres and cites Bhatt–Lurie §§7–8; the restriction to X_et is a formal step.

items.name: Syntomic complexes away from p
items.statement: For any scheme X the restriction of Z/p^n(i)_X to X[1/p] is μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}; if p is invertible on X then Z/p^n(i)_X ≃ μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}.
items.note: Part of Bhatt–Lurie's definition of the syntomic complexes of arbitrary schemes, planned with them in PR.4.

items.name: Syntomic complexes of regular F_p-schemes
items.statement: If X is a regular F_p-scheme, Z/p^n(i)_X ≃ W_nΩ^i_{log,X}[−i], where W_nΩ^i_log is the logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaf of Milne, Illusie and Gros ([BMS19, Sec. 8]).
items.note: PR.4 plans the logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparison under BMS2's hypotheses; CR.4 builds W_nΩ and dlog. The regular (not only smooth) case follows by Néron–Popescu (item 069).

items.name: Syntomic cohomology of p-henselian rings as a filtered Frobenius eigenspace
items.statement: If X = Spec(R) for a p-henselian animated ring R, then Z_p(i)(X) = eq(can, φ_i : N^{≥i}Δ_X{i} ⇉ Δ_X{i}) (equation (1)), where Δ_X{i} is the Breuil–Kisin twisted absolute prismatic cohomology, N^{≥*} the Nygaard filtration, φ_i the divided Frobenius and can the inclusion. For i ≤ p − 2, or up to isogeny, this agrees with the syntomic cohomology of Fontaine–Messing and Kato ([AMMN22, Sec. 6]).
items.note: The Fontaine–Messing comparison is AMMN's Theorem F, routed by that extraction.

items.name: The gluing square defining syntomic cohomology of an arbitrary ring
items.statement: For a commutative ring R with p-henselization R^h_(p) there is a fibre square with top row Z/p^n(i)(Spec R) → RΓ_et(Spec R[1/p], μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) and bottom row Z/p^n(i)(Spec R^h_(p)) → RΓ_et(Spec R^h_(p)[1/p], μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}); the bottom map comes from the prismatic logarithm and the étale comparison [BL22a, §8.3], and the square is the definition of the top-left corner in [BL22a, §8.4].

items.name: Syntomic complexes in weights zero and one
items.statement: For any scheme X, Z/p^n(0)_X is the constant sheaf Z/p^n, and Z/p^n(1)_X is the derived pushforward of μ_{p^n} from the fppf site to the étale site, equivalently the fibre of p^n : G_m → G_m in D(X_et) ([BL22a, Prop. 8.4.14]). In particular there is a Kummer map O_X^× → H^1(Z/p^n(1)_X), and by cup product a symbol map (O_X^×)^{⊗i} → H^i(Z/p^n(i)_X).

items.name: p-quasisyntomic rings
items.statement: A ring R is p-quasisyntomic if it has bounded p-power torsion and L_{R/Z} ⊗^L_R R/pR ∈ D(R/pR) has Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; any locally complete intersection noetherian ring is p-quasisyntomic ([BMS19, Sec. 4], [BL22a, App. C]).

items.name: Syntomic complexes via algebraic K-theory
items.statement: For a p-quasisyntomic scheme X and i ≥ 0, Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D(X_et, Z/p^n) is the derived pushforward from the syntomic site to the étale site of the sheafification of the presheaf K_{2i}(−; Z/p^n).
items.note: Stated without proof ('a consequence of [BMS19] and rigidity [Gab92, Sus83, CMM21] ... discussed in more detail separately'); not used in the paper. Its inputs are BMS2's motivic filtration on TC, Bhatt–Scholze's Theorem 14.1 and the Clausen–Mathew–Morrow rigidity theorem.

items.name: Connectivity and left Kan extension of the syntomic complexes (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus)
items.statement: For every scheme X and i ≥ 0, Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D^{[0,i]}(X_et, Z/p^n) ([AMMN22, Cor. 5.43]); in particular Z/p^n(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤i} for R strictly henselian local. On p-henselian rings the functor F_p(i)(−) is left Kan extended from (p-henselizations of) smooth Z-algebras ([AMMN22, Th. 5.1], [BL22a, Prop. 7.4.8]).
items.locator: §1.2, p. 3; §5.3, p. 22; proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 24
items.note: AMMN's Theorem G (items 049–050 of PAPER-ANTIEAU-MATHEW-MORROW-ETAL-22), routed there as a source of PR.3–PR.4.

items.name: The comparison map with truncated p-adic nearby cycles
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 and j : X[1/p] ⊂ X, adjunction and Example 1.2 give Z/p^n(i)_X → Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}), which factors through τ^{≤i}Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) because Z/p^n(i)_X ∈ D^{[0,i]}; together with the symbol map (O_X^×)^{⊗i} → H^i(Z/p^n(i)_X) (surjective by Proposition 5.5) it identifies the image of H^i(Z/p^n(i)_X) → R^i j_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) with the subsheaf generated by O_X^×-symbols.

items.name: F-smooth rings and schemes
items.statement: A p-quasisyntomic ring A is F-smooth if for each i ∈ Z_{≥0} the map φ_i : N^iΔ_A → Δ̄_A{i} in D(A) induced by the Frobenius has fibre with p-complete Tor-amplitude in degrees ≥ i + 2, and the Nygaard filtration on Δ̄_A{i} (equivalently on Δ_A{i}) is complete. The condition depends only on the p-completion of A. A p-quasisyntomic scheme is F-smooth if it is covered by spectra of F-smooth rings (F-smoothness is preserved by Zariski localization, Proposition 4.7).
items.note: The printed Definition 4.1 cites Proposition 4.6 for Zariski localization; the statement is Proposition 4.7 (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Theorem 1.8: syntomic complexes of F-smooth schemes are p-adic étale Tate twists
items.statement: Let X be a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme (for example a regular scheme flat over Z) and i ≥ 0. The comparison map Z/p^n(i)_X → τ^{≤i}Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in degrees < i; on H^i it is injective, with image the subsheaf generated by symbols under (O_X^×)^{⊗i} → R^i j_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}).

items.name: The fibre square for Z/p^n(i)_X
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.8, there is a fibre square in D(X_et) with top row Z/p^n(i)_X → τ^{≤i}Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}), bottom row image((O_X^×)^{⊗i} → R^i j_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}))[−i] → R^i j_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i})[−i], and vertical maps the projections to the top cohomology; that is, Z/p^n(i)_X is obtained from the truncated p-adic nearby cycles by replacing the top cohomology sheaf with its subsheaf generated by O_X^×-symbols. On schemes smooth, or regular with semistable reduction, over a DVR this identifies Z/p^n(i)_X with Sato's p-adic étale Tate twists.

items.name: The quasisyntomic site qSyn_{Z_p} and its basis qrsPerfd_{Z_p}
items.statement: qSyn_{Z_p} has objects the p-complete, p-torsion-free rings A with L_{A/Z_p} ⊗^L_A A/p ∈ D(A/p) of Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], with the quasisyntomic topology; the p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (those objects admitting a surjection from a perfectoid ring) form a basis qrsPerfd_{Z_p}.
items.note: The paper works with the p-torsion-free version of the site of [BMS19, Sec. 4].

items.name: The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring and its Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} there is a prism (Δ_R, φ, I) with a map R → Δ_R/I, initial among such prisms; Δ̄_R := Δ_R/I is the Hodge–Tate cohomology of R.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin twists and divided Frobenius on them
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} there is an invertible Δ_R-module Δ_R{1} with a φ-linear map φ_1 : Δ_R{1} → I^{−1}Δ_R{1} whose φ-linearization is an isomorphism, and Δ̄_R{1} ≅ I/I^2; Δ_R{n} := Δ_R{1}^{⊗n} with φ_n : Δ_R{n} → I^{−n}Δ_R{n}. These give p-complete sheaves on qrsPerfd with vanishing higher cohomology, hence D(Z_p)-valued sheaves on qSyn_{Z_p}, extended to animated rings by animation ([BL22a, Sec. 4.5]).
items.locator: Construction 2.1(2) and the paragraph after it, p. 5

items.name: The Nygaard filtration and the graded divided Frobenius
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p}, N^{≥i}Δ_R := φ^{−1}(I^iΔ_R) is a descending multiplicative filtration with graded pieces N^iΔ_R, and passing to associated graded terms of φ : N^{≥*}Δ_R → I^*Δ_R gives a map of graded rings ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R → ⊕_{i∈Z} (I/I^2)^{⊗i} = ⊕_{i∈Z} Δ̄_R{i}, whose components are the maps φ_i.

items.name: The prismatic logarithm
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} there is a prismatic logarithm log_Δ : T_p(R^×) → Δ_R{1} whose image consists exactly of the y ∈ Δ_R{1} with φ_1(y) = y.
items.note: Bhatt–Lurie [BL22a, §2]; CohomologyComparisons CP.6 compares it with the Kummer and dlog classes.

items.name: Syntomic sheaves Z_p(i) and their extension to all schemes
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 the D(Z_p)^{≥0}-valued sheaf Z_p(i)(−) on qrsPerfd_{Z_p} sends R to fib(can − φ_i : N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} → Δ_R{i}) [BMS19]; by [BS22, Th. 14.1] there is a basis of qrsPerfd_{Z_p} on which it is discrete. It extends by animation to all p-complete animated rings, and in [BL22a, Sec. 8] to all animated rings and schemes by gluing with the Tate twists on the generic fibre; on p-quasisyntomic rings Z_p(i)(−) is concentrated in nonnegative degrees.

items.name: The prism of Z_p^cycl and the generator of its Breuil–Kisin twist
items.statement: For R = Z_p^cycl = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧, Δ_R = Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]^∧_{(p,q−1)} and I = ([p]_q), [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1). The choice (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) gives ε ∈ T_p(R^×) such that log_Δ(ε) ∈ Δ_R{1} is divisible by q − 1 and log_Δ(ε)/(q − 1) generates Δ_R{1} ([BL22a, Sec. 2.6]).
items.note: PR.0 has the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]], [p]_q) as an acceptance example; the twist generator is Bhatt–Lurie's.

items.name: Hodge–Tate cohomology of Z_p through the Hodge–Tate stack
items.statement: The Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{Z_p}{i} is the coherent cohomology of O_{WCart^HT}{i} on WCart^HT ≃ BG_m^♯. p-torsion quasi-coherent sheaves on BG_m^♯ are F_p-vector spaces V with an endomorphism Θ whose generalized eigenvalues lie in F_p, the cohomology being fib(Θ : V → V), and O_{WCart^HT}{i}/p corresponds to Θ = i on F_p ([BL22a, Sec. 3]).

items.name: The bigraded rings of mod p Hodge–Tate and Nygaard cohomology of Z_p
items.statement: There are isomorphisms of bigraded F_p-algebras H^*(Δ̄_{Z_p}{*}/p) ≅ E(α) ⊗ P(θ^{±1}) and ⊕_{i≥0} H^*(N^iΔ_{Z_p}/p) ≅ E(α) ⊗ P(θ), with |α| = (1, p) and |θ| = (0, p) (cohomological degree first, twist second), and the map ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_{Z_p}/p → ⊕_{i∈Z} Δ̄_{Z_p}{i}/p sends α ↦ α and θ ↦ θ. In particular N^jΔ_{Z_p}/p = 0 unless p | j.

items.name: The graded divided Frobenius for a perfectoid ring
items.statement: For a p-torsion-free perfectoid ring R (so R ≅ Δ̄_R), the map ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R/p → ⊕_{i∈Z} Δ̄_R{i}/p is the inclusion ⊕_{i≥0} R{i}/p ⊂ ⊕_{i∈Z} R{i}/p, and θ maps to a generator of N^pΔ_R/p.

items.name: Inverting θ recovers mod p Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: For any animated ring A, the map of graded E_∞-F_p-algebras ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_A/p → ⊕_{i∈Z} Δ̄_A{i}/p exhibits the target as the localization of the source at θ.

items.name: The class v_1 ∈ H^0(F_p(p−1)(Z))
items.statement: Let R = Z[ζ_{p^∞}] and ε ∈ T_p(R^×) the class of (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …), viewed in H^0(Z_p(1)(R)). By flat descent [BL22a, Prop. 8.4.6] H^0(F_p(p−1)(Z)) is the equalizer of the two maps H^0(F_p(p−1)(R)) ⇉ H^0(F_p(p−1)(R ⊗ R)), and the image of ε^{p−1} lies in it; this defines v_1 ∈ H^0(F_p(p−1)(Z)), with v_1 = log_Δ(ε)^{p−1} over Z_p^cycl. For any X, v_1 gives a class in H^0(⊕_i F_p(i)(X)) that becomes a unit on X[1/p].
items.note: The key step: log_Δ(ε_1) and log_Δ(ε_2) generate the same invertible module after inverting (q_1−1)(q_2−1) in Δ_{R⊗R}/p, their ratio x is a unit with x^p = x, so x^{p−1} = 1. The class also appears in [Dri20, Prop. 8.11.2].

items.name: v_1 detects the topological class v_1
items.statement: For p > 2, the class v_1^top ∈ π_{2p−2}(S/p) gives a nonzero class in π_{2p−2}TC(Z_p; F_p) which, under the motivic spectral sequence of [BMS19], is detected up to a nonzero scalar by v_1; this is checked over O_{C_p} using ku/p ≃ TC(O_C; F_p).
items.note: A remark that plays no role in the proofs; the brief lists it as optional.

items.name: The lift θ̃ of v_1
items.statement: The image of v_1 in H^0(N^{≥p−1}Δ_{Z_p}{p−1}/p) lifts uniquely to θ̃ ∈ H^0(N^{≥p}Δ_{Z_p}{p−1}/p), because N^{p−1}Δ_{Z_p}/p = 0 (Construction 2.4).

items.name: θ̃ maps to a generator of H^0(N^pΔ_{Z_p}/p)
items.statement: The image of θ̃ in H^0(N^pΔ_{Z_p}/p) is a generator; after normalization it is θ.
items.note: Proof over Z_p^cycl: v_1 = log_Δ(ε)^{p−1} is (q−1)^{p−1} ≡ (q^{1/p}−1)^{p(p−1)} mod p times a generator, and the Nygaard filtration is by powers of [p]_{q^{1/p}} ≡ (q^{1/p}−1)^{p−1}.

items.name: A direct prismatic construction of v_1
items.statement: For a p-torsion-free prism (A, I, φ) with A/I p-torsion-free and a generator y of A/p{1}, the element (y/φ_1(y))·y^{p−1} ∈ I·A/p{p−1} is fixed by φ_{p−1} and independent of y. These elements give an element of H^0(F_p(p−1)(Z_p)), which reproduces the image of v_1 up to a scalar (checked on the prism of Z_p^cycl).

items.name: The Nygaard filtration on Hodge–Tate cohomology
items.statement: For R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p}, the image of N^{≥*}Δ_R is a filtered ring N^{≥*}Δ̄_R. Since I maps to (p) under Δ_R → R, gr^*Δ̄_R ≅ ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R/p (equation (3)); the composite R → Δ̄_R → gr^0Δ̄_R ≅ R/p is Frobenius, so as R-modules gr^iΔ̄_R ≅ N^iΔ_R/p^{(−1)} (restriction along Frobenius) and gr^0Δ̄_R ≅ R/p^{(−1)} (equation (4)). The same holds for Δ̄_R{i}, and by descent and left Kan extension N^{≥*}Δ̄_A is defined as a commutative algebra in the filtered derived ∞-category for every animated ring A.

items.name: θ detects p in the Nygaard filtration
items.statement: The element p ∈ H^0(Δ̄_{Z_p}) lies in Nygaard filtration p and is detected there, up to a unit, by θ ∈ H^0(N^pΔ_{Z_p}/p). For R = Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}]^∧, Δ_R = W(R^♭), I = (p − [p^♭]), N^{≥i}Δ_R = (p − [p^{♭,1/p}])^i, whose image in Δ̄_R = R is (p^{i/p}).

items.name: The twisted Nygaard filtration on Δ̄_R{i}/p
items.statement: For any animated ring R there is a natural decreasing multiplicative Z_{≥0}^{op}-indexed filtration Ñ^{≥*}(Δ̄_R/p) with gr^* ≅ (⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R/p)/θ, θ in grading p (equation (5)); for each i ∈ Z there is a module filtration Ñ^{≥*}(Δ̄_R{i}/p) with gr^j ≅ cofib(θ : N^{j−p}Δ_R/p → N^jΔ_R/p), N^j = 0 for j < 0 (equation (6)).

items.name: Completeness of the twisted Nygaard filtration
items.statement: The twisted Nygaard filtration Ñ^{≥*}(Δ̄_R{i}/p) is complete if and only if the Nygaard filtration N^{≥*}Δ̄_R{i} is complete.

items.name: Relatively perfect maps of animated rings
items.statement: An animated A-algebra B is relatively perfect over A if the square with horizontal maps A/p → B/p and vertical maps the Frobenius of A/p and of B/p is a pushout of animated rings. Then L_{B/A} vanishes p-adically ([Bha12, Cor. 3.8]), so L_{A/Z} ⊗_A B → L_{B/Z} is a p-adic equivalence.

items.name: Animated and classical relative perfectness agree for flat maps
items.statement: If R → S is a flat map of animated F_p-algebras, it is relatively perfect in the animated sense if and only if π_0(R) → π_0(S) is relatively perfect classically. Hence for discrete rings A → B with B p-completely flat over A, relative perfectness can be tested on the ordinary quotients A/pA → B/pB.

items.name: Base change of Nygaard filtrations along relatively perfect maps
items.statement: If A → B is a relatively perfect map of animated rings, the natural maps N^{≥*}Δ̄_A{i} ⊗_A B → N^{≥*}Δ̄_B{i} and the analogous maps of twisted Nygaard filtrations on Δ̄_{(−)}{i}/p are equivalences after p-completion, and N^iΔ_A ⊗_A B → N^iΔ_B is a p-adic equivalence for each i.
items.note: Uses the absolute conjugate filtrations [BL22a, Sec. 4.5] and the Nygaard fibre sequence [BL22a, Rem. 5.5.8]; relative perfectness, not just vanishing of L_{B/A}, is needed because of the Frobenius restrictions in (3).

items.name: Automatic internal gradings
items.statement: Let F be a functor from qrsPerfd_{Z_p} to p-complete abelian groups with bounded p-power torsion, with natural R-module structures such that F(R) ⊗_R R[t^{1/p^∞}] → F(R⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩) is a p-adic equivalence. Then for R' ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} with a (p-complete) Z[1/p]_{≥0}-grading, F(R') inherits a Z[1/p]_{≥0}-grading: y is homogeneous of degree i iff coact(y) = y ⊗ t^i, where coact : R' → R'⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩ sends x ∈ R'_i to x ⊗ t^i.

items.name: Weight gradings on Hodge–Tate and Nygaard cohomology
items.statement: For a Z[1/p]_{≥0}-graded animated ring R, N^{≥*}Δ̄_R{i} is naturally a Z[1/p]_{≥0}-graded object of the p-complete derived category, and so is N^iΔ_R for i ≥ 0 (quasisyntomic descent, animation, Remark 3.8 and Proposition 3.7 for Z → Z[t^{1/p^∞}]). Equivalently the Hodge–Tate stack of G_m^perf is G_m^perf × WCart^HT, so a G_m^perf-action on X induces one on WCart^HT_X.

items.name: Weights of Nygaard pieces of nonnegatively graded rings
items.statement: If R is Z[1/p]_{≥0}-graded and concentrated in degrees Z_{≥0}, then N^iΔ_R and Δ̄_R{i} are concentrated in weights Z_{≥0}, while the graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration on Δ̄_R lie in weights (1/p)Z_{≥0}.

items.name: Nygaard pieces of a polynomial ring
items.statement: Let R be a p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid ring and A^* = ⊕_{i≥0} (N^iΔ_R ⊗_R R[x])^∧. Then H^0(⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_{R[x]}) ≅ A^* and H^1(⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_{R[x]}) ≅ A^{*−1} as graded A^*-modules, with generators in weights 0 and 1 for the weight grading |x| = 1; the H^1 generator is dx via N^1Δ_S ≃ L^∧_{S/Z}[−1].

items.name: Hodge–Tate cohomology of a polynomial ring with its Nygaard filtration
items.statement: Let R ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p} be p-torsion-free and A^{≥*} the p-completion of N^{≥*}Δ̄_R ⊗_R R[x]. Then as A^{≥*}-modules H^0(N^{≥*}Δ̄_{R[x]}) ≅ A^{≥*} and H^1(N^{≥*}Δ̄_{R[x]}) ≅ A^{≥*−1}{−1} ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^{p−1} A^{≥*−1}/A^{≥*}. For the weight grading with |x| = 1, the generator of H^0 has weight 0, that of A^{≥*−1}{−1} (the class dx) weight 1, and the ith copy of A^{≥*−1}/A^{≥*} (the boundary of x^{i/p}) weight i/p.
items.note: Equation (10) in the proof prints A^{≥*}{−1} for the first summand; the statement (8) is right (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Nygaard pieces of a quotient by x
items.statement: For any animated Z[x]-algebra R there is a natural fibre sequence of graded ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R-modules (⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_R)/x → ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_{R/x} → ⊕_{i≥0} N^{i−1}Δ_{R/x}.

items.name: A finite filtration on N^{≥*}Δ̄_{B[x]}/x
items.statement: For B ∈ qrsPerfd_{Z_p}, naturally in B, N^{≥*}Δ̄_{B[x]}/x has a finite filtration by N^{≥*}Δ̄_{B[x]}/x-modules with graded pieces N^{≥*}Δ̄_B, p − 1 copies of (N^{≥*−1}Δ̄_B/N^{≥*}Δ̄_B)[−1], and N^{≥*−1}Δ̄_B{−1}[−1] (the weight 0, i/p and 1 parts).

items.name: The Nygaard-filtered Hodge–Tate cohomology of A/x
items.statement: For any animated Z[x]-algebra A and i ∈ Z, N^{≥*}Δ̄_A/x{i} has a natural finite filtration with graded pieces N^{≥*}Δ̄_{A/x}{i}, p − 1 copies of (N^{≥*−1}Δ̄_{A/x}/N^{≥*}Δ̄_{A/x}){i}[−1], and N^{≥*−1}Δ̄_{A/x}{i−1}[−1].

items.name: The fibre sequence for Hodge–Tate cohomology of a quotient
items.statement: For any animated Z[x]-algebra R there is a natural fibre sequence Δ̄_R/x{i} → Δ̄_{R/x}{i} → Δ̄_{R/x}{i−1}.
items.note: Also obtainable from the Hodge–Tate stack of the affine line [BL22b, Ex. 9.1].

items.name: Bhatt–Lurie's Nygaard fibre sequence and the first Nygaard piece
items.statement: For an animated ring S, N^1Δ_S ≃ L^∧_{S/Z}[−1] ([BL22a, Prop. 5.5.12]); N^iΔ_S ∈ D^{≤i}(Z_p) ([BL22a, Rem. 5.5.9]); and there are fibre sequences N^iΔ_S → Fil_i^conj Ω^{D̸}_S → Fil_{i−1}^conj Ω^{D̸}_S with second map Θ + i, where Ω^{D̸}_S is the diffracted Hodge complex with its conjugate filtration and Sen operator Θ ([BL22a, Rem. 5.5.8, Cons. 4.7.1, Not. 4.7.2]).

items.name: Nygaard graded pieces and the conjugate filtration over a perfectoid base
items.statement: For S an algebra over a perfectoid ring R_0 (trivializing the twists), φ_i : N^iΔ_S → Δ̄_S identifies N^iΔ_S with the ith stage Fil_i^conj Δ̄_S of the conjugate filtration ([BS22, Th. 12.2]).

items.name: The Hodge–Tate comparison
items.statement: For S smooth over a perfectoid ring R_0, H^i(Δ̄_S) ≅ Ω^i_{S/R_0}{−i}, the class dx arising as the image of x under the boundary of Δ̄_S{1} → Δ_S/I^2 → Δ̄_S ([BS22, Th. 4.11, Cons. 4.9]).

items.name: André's lemma
items.statement: Every perfectoid ring R admits a p-completely faithfully flat map to a perfectoid ring in which every element has a compatible system of p-power roots ([BS22, Th. 7.14]); used to adjoin p^{1/p}.

items.name: Conjugate filtration on p-adic derived de Rham cohomology
items.statement: For F_p-algebras (and p-adically), derived de Rham cohomology carries the conjugate filtration with graded pieces the Frobenius-twisted exterior powers of the cotangent complex ([Bha12, Prop. 3.5]); if B is relatively perfect over A then L_{B/A} vanishes p-adically ([Bha12, Cor. 3.8]).

items.name: p-complete Tor-amplitude
items.statement: For A p-quasisyntomic, M ∈ D(A) has p-complete Tor-amplitude in degrees ≥ r if M ⊗^L_A N ∈ D^{≥r}(A) for every discrete A/p-module N ([BMS19, Def. 4.1]).

items.name: Weakly F-smooth rings
items.statement: A p-quasisyntomic ring A is weakly F-smooth if for each i the fibre of θ : N^iΔ_A/p → N^{i+p}Δ_A/p in D(A) has p-complete Tor-amplitude in degrees ≥ i + 1. If A is also p-torsion-free, this fibre is concentrated in degrees ≥ i + 2.

items.name: F-smooth rings are weakly F-smooth
items.statement: If a p-quasisyntomic ring A is F-smooth, then A is weakly F-smooth.

items.name: F-smoothness as weak F-smoothness plus localization at θ
items.statement: A p-quasisyntomic ring A is F-smooth if and only if it is weakly F-smooth and the map of graded E_∞-rings ⊕_i φ_i : ⊕_{i≥0} N^iΔ_A/p → ⊕_{i∈Z} Δ̂̄_A{i}/p, whose target is the Nygaard-completed Hodge–Tate cohomology mod p, exhibits the target as the localization of the source at θ.

items.name: Stability of weak F-smoothness
items.statement: Weakly F-smooth rings are closed under filtered colimits and étale localization inside p-quasisyntomic rings, and weak F-smoothness can be checked étale-locally.

items.name: Essential constancy of the twisted Nygaard filtration
items.statement: If A is weakly F-smooth, then for fixed n, H^n(fib(θ : N^jΔ_A/p → N^{j+p}Δ_A/p)) = 0 for j ≫ 0; hence the twisted Nygaard filtration on Δ̄_A{i}/p is essentially constant in each cohomological degree, with constants independent of A.

items.name: F-smoothness is stable under filtered colimits
items.statement: The property of being F-smooth is stable under filtered colimits.
items.note: Titled 'under filtered colimits and étale localization', but only filtered colimits are stated and proved; étale localization is Proposition 4.7 (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: F-smoothness and relatively perfect flat maps
items.statement: Let A be p-quasisyntomic and B a p-completely flat, relatively perfect A-algebra. If A is F-smooth then so is B; conversely if B is p-completely faithfully flat over A and B is F-smooth then so is A. In particular F-smoothness is étale local and passes to étale algebras.
items.note: The flatness hypothesis is not in the characteristic-p analogue [BLM21, Prop. 9.5.11]; the authors expect it to be unnecessary.

items.name: F-smoothness of polynomial rings
items.statement: If a p-quasisyntomic ring A is F-smooth, then A[x] is F-smooth.

items.name: F-smoothness of algebras smooth mod p
items.statement: Let A be p-quasisyntomic and B a p-completely flat A-algebra with A/p → B/p smooth. If A is F-smooth then so is B.
items.note: The printed proof combines Propositions 4.8 and 4.6; the étale step needs Proposition 4.7 (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: F-smoothness is local on Spec
items.statement: A p-quasisyntomic ring A is F-smooth if and only if A_𝔭 is F-smooth for every 𝔭 ∈ Spec(A).

items.name: F-smoothness and the Beilinson t-structure
items.statement: Let A be F-smooth and Δ_A^{[•]} the complete filtration of Δ_A by powers of the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf, so gr^*Δ_A^{[•]} ≃ Δ̄_A{*}. The refined Frobenius φ_A : N^{≥*}Δ_A → Δ_A^{[•]} induces N^iΔ_A ≃ τ^{≤i}gr^iΔ_A^{[•]}, and identifies its source with the connective cover of its target for the Beilinson t-structure on the filtered derived category ([BMS19, Sec. 5.4]).
items.note: The Beilinson t-structure and décalage are imported from AInfCohomology AI.1 (Lη).

items.name: F-smoothness over a perfectoid base (after Bouis)
items.statement: Let R_0 be perfectoid and A a quasisyntomic R_0-algebra. Then A is F-smooth if and only if (1) L^∧_{A/R_0} is a p-completely flat A-module and (2) the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology LΩ_{A/R_0} is Hodge-complete.

items.name: Hodge-completeness of derived de Rham cohomology and Nygaard-completeness
items.statement: Over the perfect prism of a perfectoid ring R_0, the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology LΩ_{A/R_0} is Hodge-complete if and only if the derived prismatic cohomology Δ_A is Nygaard-complete ([BMS19, Th. 7.2(5)]).

items.name: Cartier smooth F_p-algebras
items.statement: A quasisyntomic F_p-algebra A is Cartier smooth if (1) L_{A/F_p} is a flat discrete A-module and (2) the inverse Cartier map C^{−1} : Ω^i_{A/F_p} → H^i(Ω^*_{A/F_p}) is an isomorphism for all i ≥ 0 (Ω^* the classical de Rham complex) ([KM21, KST21]).
items.note: Kelly–Morrow and Kerz–Strunk–Tamme show Z/p^n(i) ≃ W_nΩ^i_log[−i] on Cartier smooth F_p-algebras; Theorem 1.8 is presented as its mixed-characteristic analogue.

items.name: F-smooth equals Cartier smooth in characteristic p
items.statement: A quasisyntomic F_p-algebra is F-smooth if and only if it is Cartier smooth.

items.name: Regular rings are F-smooth
items.statement: Every regular noetherian ring is F-smooth.
items.locator: Theorem 4.15, first claim, p. 16; proof p. 17
items.note: Characteristic p: Cartier smoothness via Néron–Popescu (or [BLM21, Sec. 9.5]). Unramified regular rings were largely treated in [BL22a, Prop. 5.7.9, 5.8.2]. Mixed characteristic: induction on dimension with Proposition 4.16 and x ∈ 𝔪 ∖ 𝔪^2.

items.name: p-complete noetherian F-smooth rings are regular
items.statement: If A is a p-complete noetherian ring that is F-smooth, then A is regular.
items.locator: Theorem 4.15, second claim, p. 16; proof p. 18

items.name: Néron–Popescu desingularization
items.statement: A regular noetherian F_p-algebra is a filtered colimit of smooth F_p-algebras; more generally a regular homomorphism of noetherian rings is a filtered colimit of smooth ones.
items.note: Used to show regular F_p-algebras are Cartier smooth; the same statement is routed by the Česnavičius extraction (PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-22/popescu) as a source of SF.0.

items.name: F-smoothness from a nonzerodivisor
items.statement: Let A be p-quasisyntomic and x ∈ A a nonzerodivisor. If A/x and A[1/x] are F-smooth, then A is F-smooth.

items.name: Cartier smooth reduction implies F-smooth
items.statement: If A is p-quasisyntomic and p-torsion-free and A/p is Cartier smooth, then A is F-smooth.

items.name: A cotangent-complex criterion for regularity
items.statement: A complete intersection local ring (A, 𝔪, k) is regular if and only if H^{−1}(L_{A/Z} ⊗_A k) → H^{−1}(L_{k/Z}) is injective.
items.note: Equivalent, by the transitivity triangle for Z → A → k and L_{k/Z} ∈ D^{[−1,0]}, to H^{−2}(L_{k/A}) = 0, which is André's regularity criterion (item 073). The complete-intersection hypothesis is not used.

items.name: André's regularity criterion
items.statement: A noetherian local ring (A, 𝔪, k) is regular if and only if H^{−2}(L_{k/A}) = 0, i.e. the André–Quillen homology D_2(k|A, k) vanishes ([Iye07, Prop. 8.12]).

items.name: Avramov's absolute complete-intersection criterion
items.statement: A noetherian local ring (A, 𝔪, k) with L_{A/Z} ⊗^L_A k ∈ D^{[−1,0]}(k) is a complete intersection ([Avr99, Prop. 1.8]); in particular a p-complete noetherian local p-quasisyntomic ring with residue characteristic p is one.
items.locator: Proof that F-smoothness implies regularity, p. 18

items.name: Décalage for derived exterior powers
items.statement: For M ∈ D(k) concentrated in degree −1, ∧^p(M) ≃ Γ^p(H^{−1}M)[p]; in particular H^{−p}(∧^p L) = Γ^p H^{−1}(L) for L of Tor-amplitude [−1, 0] ([Ill71, §4.3.2]).
items.note: DD.0 plans derived symmetric, divided and exterior power functors.

items.name: The fibre sequence for cofib(θ) and Nygaard level p of polynomial rings
items.statement: For an animated ring B there is a fibre sequence in D(B/p), cofib(θ : B/p → N^pΔ_B/p) → ∧^p L_{(B/p)/F_p}[−p] → B/p (equation (17)). For B a polynomial Z-algebra, H^*(N^pΔ_B) is B/p in degree 1, Ω̂^p_{B/Z} in degree p and 0 otherwise, and θ : B/p → N^pΔ_B/p is an isomorphism on H^0.

items.name: Regularity of complete intersections via θ
items.statement: Let A be a complete intersection local noetherian ring with residue field k of characteristic p. Then A is regular if and only if cofib(θ : A/p → N^pΔ_A/p) ⊗^L_{A/p} k ∈ D^{≥1}(k) (which holds when A is F-smooth); reductions mod p are derived.

items.name: F-finiteness: Kunz's criterion
items.statement: A noetherian F_p-algebra S is F-finite if it is finitely generated over its pth powers; a noetherian local F_p-algebra is F-finite if and only if its residue field is F-finite and it is excellent ([Kun76, Cor. 2.6]).

items.name: F-finiteness and almost perfect cotangent complex
items.statement: A noetherian F_p-algebra S is F-finite if and only if L_{S/F_p} ∈ D(S) is almost perfect ([DM17, Th. 3.6], [Lur18, Th. 3.5.1]).

items.name: The Cohen structure theorem
items.statement: A complete regular local ring R of residue characteristic p with residue field k and dim R = r admits a surjection W[[t_1, …, t_r]] → R, W a Cohen ring for k, whose kernel is generated by a nonzerodivisor; choosing a p-basis of k, W[[t_1, …, t_r]] is p-adically formally étale over a polynomial ring over Z_p in d = r + log_p[k : k^p] variables.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate stack of a p-adic formal scheme
items.statement: For a quasisyntomic ring R, WCart^HT_{Spf R} → Spf R is the relative Hodge–Tate stack of [BL22b, Cons. 3.7], with line bundles O{i} whose cohomology is Δ̄_R{i}; if R → R' has L_{R/Z} ⊗ R' → L_{R'/Z} an isomorphism after p-completion, WCart^HT_{Spf R'} ≃ Spf R' ×_{Spf R} WCart^HT_{Spf R} ([BL22b, Rem. 3.9]).
items.note: PR.5 plans Bhatt–Lurie's Cartier–Witt stack and prismatization of p-adic formal schemes (RingStacksAndTransmutation RS.1 imports it from PR.5).

items.name: The Hodge–Tate stack of affine space
items.statement: WCart^HT_{Spf Z_p⟨x_1,…,x_d⟩} is the classifying stack of G_a^{♯d} ⋊ G_m^♯ over Spf Z_p⟨x_1,…,x_d⟩ ([BL22b, Ex. 9.1]); quasi-coherent sheaves are described by representations of G_a^♯ and G_m^♯ ([BL22a, Sec. 3.5], [BL22b, Lem. 6.7]), whence cohomological dimension ≤ d + 1.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 4.20 and Lemma 4.21, pp. 19–20

items.name: Dimension bound for the Hodge–Tate stack of a regular local ring
items.statement: Let R be a p-complete regular local ring with residue field k such that R/pR is F-finite, and d = dim R + log_p[k : k^p]. Then WCart^HT_{Spf R} has cohomological dimension ≤ d; in particular Δ̄_R{i} ∈ D^{≤d}(Z_p) for each i.
items.note: Verifies [BL22b, Conj. 10.1] under F-finiteness. Proof: reduce to R complete; Δ̄_R{i} is 𝔪-adically complete by Nygaard completeness (Theorem 4.15) and induct with Corollary 3.16; bound cd by d + 1 via Cohen's theorem and Lemma 4.21, then kill H^{d+1} using generation by the O{n}/p.

items.name: Affineness of the Hodge–Tate stack of a hypersurface
items.statement: For a quasisyntomic ring R and a nonzerodivisor t ∈ R, the map WCart^HT_{Spf(R/t)} → Spf(R/t) ×_{Spf R} WCart^HT_{Spf R} is affine.

items.name: Bhatt–Lurie's étale comparison and left Kan extension of syntomic cohomology
items.statement: For a scheme over Z[ζ_{p^∞}], ⊕_i Z_p(i)(X) → ⊕_i Z_p(i)(X[1/p]) exhibits the target as the localization at ε ∈ H^0(Z_p(1)(Z[ζ_{p^∞}])) ([BL22a, Th. 8.5.1]). The functor R ↦ ⊕_i F_p(i)(R) is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras ([BL22a, Prop. 8.4.10], via the fibre sequence [BL22a, Rem. 8.4.8]) and satisfies flat descent ([BL22a, Prop. 8.4.6]).

items.name: The étale comparison: inverting v_1
items.statement: For every qcqs derived scheme X, the map of graded E_∞-F_p-algebras ⊕_{i∈Z} F_p(i)(X) → ⊕_{i∈Z} F_p(i)(X[1/p]) exhibits the target as the localization of the source at v_1; so colim(F_p(i)(X) →^{v_1} F_p(i+p−1)(X) →^{v_1} …) ≃ RΓ_et(X[1/p], F_p(i)).
items.note: Deduced from [BL22a, Th. 8.5.1] over Z[ζ_{p^∞}]: for p-quasisyntomic X by descent; in general by showing that R ↦ RΓ_et(Spec R[1/p], μ_p^{⊗i}) is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras and taking Z_p^×-invariants.

items.name: The generic-fibre comparison for F-smooth rings
items.statement: Let A be a p-torsion-free p-quasisyntomic F-smooth ring. For each i, F_p(i)(A) → F_p(i)(A[1/p]) = RΓ_et(Spec A[1/p], F_p(i)) has fibre in D^{≥i+1}(F_p).
items.note: Over a perfectoid base, also [Bou22, Th. 4.14]. The proof shows v_1 : F_p(i)(A) → F_p(i+p−1)(A) has fibre in D^{≥i+1}, using F_p(i)(A) = eq(N^{≥i}Δ_A{i}/p ⇉ Δ_A{i}/p) (printed with p − 1 for i, sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Multiplication by θ̃ on Nygaard filtrations
items.statement: Let A be p-torsion-free, p-quasisyntomic and F-smooth. For each i, j the fibre of multiplication by θ̃, N^{≥j}Δ_A{i}/p → N^{≥j+p}Δ_A{i+p−1}/p, lies in D^{≥j+2}(F_p).

items.name: The filtered divided Frobenius mod p
items.statement: Let A be p-torsion-free, p-quasisyntomic and F-smooth. For each i ∈ Z the Frobenius φ_i : N^{≥i}Δ_A{i}/p → Δ_A{i}/p has fibre in D^{≥i+2}(F_p).

items.name: Symbolic generation of the top syntomic cohomology
items.statement: For any strictly henselian local ring R, the symbol map (R^×)^{⊗i} → H^i(Z/p^n(i)(R)) is surjective.

items.name: Bloch–Kato: p-adic nearby cycles are generated by symbols
items.statement: Let X be smooth over a henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0, p), j : X_K ⊂ X, i : Y ⊂ X the generic and special fibres, and M^q_n = i^*R^q j_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗q}). Then M^q_n is generated étale-locally by symbols: the map i^*j_*(O_{X_K}^×)^{⊗q} → M^q_n given by the Kummer map and cup products is surjective ([BK86, Th. (1.4)]).
items.locator: §5.3, equation (28) and the sentence after it, p. 23 (printed as [BK86, Th. 14.1]); footnote 2, p. 3
items.note: The printed citation 'Th. 14.1' should read Th. (1.4) (sourceIssues E5). Footnote 2 cites also [Hyo88, SS20] for symbol generation in wider settings.

items.name: Bloch–Kato's filtration on M^q_1 in the unramified case
items.statement: With notation as above and e = 1 (so e′ = p/(p−1)), the Bloch–Kato filtration gives, for R strictly henselian local ind-smooth over Z, a short exact sequence 0 → Ω^{q−1}_{R/p} → H^q(Spec R[1/p], μ_p^{⊗q}) → Ω^q_{R/p,log} ⊕ Ω^{q−1}_{R/p,log} → 0, where the first map is ρ_1 (x dlog y_1 ∧ … ↦ {1 + p x̃, ỹ_1, …}) and the second sends {r_1, …, r_q} ↦ (dlog r̄_1 ∧ … ∧ dlog r̄_q, 0) and {r_1, …, r_{q−1}, p} ↦ (0, dlog r̄_1 ∧ … ∧ dlog r̄_{q−1}) for r_j ∈ R^× ([BK86, Cor. (1.4.1), (4.3), (6.6)]).

items.name: The Bloch–Kato residue map
items.statement: There is a surjective residue map of étale F_p-sheaves res : M^q → Ω^{q−1}_{Y,log} (and, for n ≥ 1, M^q_n → W_nΩ^{q−1}_{Y,log}), the second component of gr^0 M^q_n ≅ W_nΩ^q_{Y,log} ⊕ W_nΩ^{q−1}_{Y,log} ([BK86, (6.6)]).

items.name: Symbols from R form the kernel of the residue
items.statement: If R is a strictly henselian local ring ind-smooth over Z, the kernel of the surjective residue map H^i(Spec R[1/p], μ_p^{⊗i}) → Ω^{i−1}_{R/p,log} is the subgroup generated by symbols from R, i.e. the image of (R^×)^{⊗i} under the symbol map (R[1/p]^×)^{⊗i} ↠ H^i(Spec R[1/p], μ_p^{⊗i}).

items.name: Natural maps F_p(i)(R) → F_p(i−1)(R/p)[−1] vanish
items.statement: Any natural map F_p(i)(R) → F_p(i−1)(R/p)[−1] defined on p-henselian ind-smooth Z-algebras R vanishes.
items.note: Proof: extend by left Kan extension to quasisyntomic Z_p-algebras; the source is discrete as a quasisyntomic sheaf ([BS22, Th. 14.1], printed as Th. 4.1, sourceIssues E4) and the target lives in degree 1. F_p(i−1)(R/p)[−1] = RΓ_et(Spec R/p, Ω^{i−1}_log)[−i] is [BMS19, Sec. 8].

items.name: The Steinberg relation for Kummer symbols
items.statement: If u and 1 − u are units on a scheme on which n is invertible, the cup product of their Kummer classes vanishes in H^2(−, μ_n^{⊗2}); in particular (1 + πa) ⊗ (−πa) and π ⊗ (−π) map to zero ([Tat76, Th. 3.1]).
items.note: M.5 constructs the Galois symbol K^M_*(F)/n → H^*(F, μ_n^{⊗*}), which requires the Steinberg relation; the scheme-level statement follows from the universal case over Z[1/n][u, u^{−1}, (1−u)^{−1}].

items.name: Regular local rings are factorial
items.statement: A regular local ring is a unique factorization domain (Auslander–Buchsbaum).

items.name: Localization and hyperplane sections of regular local rings
items.statement: A localization of a regular local ring at a prime is regular; for (A, 𝔪) regular local and x ∈ 𝔪 ∖ 𝔪^2, A/x is regular local of dimension dim A − 1; a noetherian ring is regular if and only if its localizations at maximal ideals are regular; regular local rings are complete intersections.
items.locator: Proofs of Theorem 4.15 and Corollary 4.20, pp. 17–19
items.note: Mathlib defines IsRegularRing through all prime localizations; the comparison with maximal ideals is Serre's theorem, flagged as a TODO in Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean.

items.name: Regular local rings and regular rings
items.statement: A noetherian local ring is regular if its maximal ideal is generated by dim R elements; a noetherian ring is regular if all its localizations at primes are regular local rings.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean at 082e2d3: IsRegularLocalRing (spanFinrank of the maximal ideal equals ringKrullDim), IsRegularRing (every localization at a prime is regular local), with IsRegularRing instances for Dedekind domains and MvPolynomial over a regular ring (Polynomial.lean).

items.name: Sato's p-adic étale Tate twists
items.statement: Let X be a regular scheme of finite type over a Dedekind domain A whose residue fields of characteristic p are perfect, semistable over the characteristic-p points of Spec A. For n, i ≥ 0 Sato constructs 𝔗_n(i)_X ∈ D^{[0,i]}(X_et, Z/p^n) as the mapping fibre of a map from τ^{≤i}Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) to the (−i)-shift of a discrete sheaf (logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves of the special fibre) ([Sat07, §4.2]). At the strict henselization R of a characteristic-p point, the image of H^i(𝔗_1(i)_X)_x in H^i(Spec R[1/p], μ_p^{⊗i}) is the subgroup generated by the symbols from (R^×)^{⊗i} and from (1 + πR)^× ⊗ (R[1/p]^×)^{⊗(i−1)} ([Sat07, §3.4, Def. 4.2.4]). Sato conjectures [Sat07, Conj. 1.4.1] that 𝔗_n(i)_X is the étale sheafification of the motivic complexes mod p^n, which follows from [Gei04] in the smooth case.

items.name: Comparison with Geisser–Sato–Schneider
items.statement: In the setting of Sato's twists there is a canonical multiplicative equivalence 𝔗_n(i)_X ≃ Z/p^n(i)_X in D^b(X_et, Z/p^n).
items.note: The proof reduces to showing that the image of (1+πR)^× ⊗ (R[1/p]^×)^{⊗(i−1)} lies in the image of (R^×)^{⊗i}, using R[1/p]^× = π^Z ⊕ R^×; that decomposition fails at points on two or more components of the special fibre (sourceIssues E6), so the design job must supply that case.

items.name: p-adic nearby cycles of smooth schemes over a mixed-characteristic DVR
items.statement: Let K be a discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with ring of integers O_K and residue field k, and X a smooth O_K-scheme with special fibre X_k. There is a natural cofibre sequence in D(X_et, Z/p^n), Z/p^n(i)_X → τ^{≤i}Rj_*(μ_{p^n}^{⊗i}) → W_nΩ^{i−1}_{X_k,log}[−i], the second map being the Bloch–Kato residue.
items.note: Printed 'with special fiber k'; the special fibre is X_k (sourceIssues E7). Earlier versions: [Kur87] in low weights; [CN17] with denominators; [BMS19, Th. 10.1] and [CDN21] over O_C.
